title: Bad for ADHD - Has Potential
body:
I have Finch and was considering switching because with Finch you can only auto-sync one device, Habit Rabbit you can sync multiple devices. I had Study Bunny for exactly 30 minutes before deleting it. There is an ad after every, single, tiny, thing you do. The ads are over bearing and are a major distraction and frustration. Unlike the creator’s other app, Study Bunny, there is no $2.00 30-day trial to take the ads down and see if you like it. You’d have to pay at least $10 to just give it a fair shot, considering most other apps make a 7 or 30-day trial free… that’s audacious. 

I kinda vibe with the simplicity of the art style and the idea that the bunny can get sad. The bird in Finch is always just happy you’re back - it’s a reward only system rather than reward/punishment - some people won’t like that at all so Habit Rabbit has that going for it in addition to the multiple device capabilities. I almost just paid the $15 out of curiosity, excitement, and frustration, BUT I invested the app more. Even with premium, there is also no categorization other than “priority” and no recurrence assignment other than weekly.

title: Limited and Distracting
body:
The app is cute and simple, which I like. Complexity takes attention away from the point - tracking habits. However, the app did not give a tutorial to move through it and I found myself experiencing a steep learning curve with all the unlabeled icons to access checklists and habits. 

Also, right out of the gate, after the app made it clear that the game is to collect carrots by completing tasks and reinforcing good habits, it gave me a hook of watching ads for carrots. This is offered 3 times a day, offering double or triple rewards if done more than once consecutively. This feels totally counterintuitive and absolutely distracting. I want to do beneficial things in real life to earn rewards, not distract myself with mindless ads.

There are also short ads built into the app, which I guess is ok since it’s free. 

Another issue is that you can’t set more than 1 high priority goal and no more than 3 medium priority goals in the free version. Not worth it, in my opinion. There are many others out there, Habitica being a really good option for one.

The tutorial is brief, and doesn’t show nearly half of the functions the app has, including the most important one : how to add and delete habits. As a suggestion, I would suggest either making the tutorial more expansive, or having users complete a tour/guide of the app upon first download. body:

Keep track of how many times the user has reset so they can look and use that as a measure of progress. Almost like a prestige in call of duty. These suggestions aren’t even that crucial but just thought I would throw some thoughts your way!

title: The only productivity app I like.
body:
I’ve tried a lot of productivity/habit-building apps. This is the ONLY one I’ve stuck with. Not only that, but I genuinely enjoy using it. The personalization (naming/customization of rabbit and their home) and aesthetic UI make me want to come back every day. But what really makes it work is the carefully crafted gamification. 

It manages to toe the delicate lines between simplicity and longevity. It’s simple enough to quickly check off habits throughout the day. The rewards are numerous enough and balanced just right so that you can see significant progress with every habit checked, but it isn’t too fast (or too slow). 

I’ve used Habit Rabbit for two weeks now and I have already built several habits into my routine that I’ve otherwise struggled to do routinely - for YEARS. (Flossed every night this week instead of putting it off because I could always do it tomorrow instead. Cleaned the dishes and put them away as I used them instead of letting them pile up in the sink.)

Whether you want to start something new or hold yourself accountable for things you currently struggle with, GET THIS LIL RABBIT.

title: Good, but Bug?
body:
Now, the three stars is for a potential bug. There is no way to turn off notifications if you set them up. When you press on a habit, it takes you to the screen with the habit info. Then press the bell and that brings you to the notifications. Now, it has a little button you press at the top for notifications, that I assume turns off the notifications, but it doesn't work. 

 I love the app. I use it almost every day! It lets you see this week and last weeks' progress in habit formation. It also records statistically how many habits you complete monthly. I think it's very helpful for keeping on track. Plus, seeing your progress is such a great motivator to keep your streak up! And decorating the rabbit's house is a cute and fun little project. It is extremely satisfying to completely clean up a room. 

 As a suggestion, maybe every week or day a new mess appears in a random completed room? Because habits require upkeep, like the rabbit's house. I haven't quite finished the last room, but there doesn't seem to be a lot of uses for the coins you build up, when you get to the end. So maybe adding some random tidy-up tasks could help. 

 I used vacation mode several times in the past two months, but I still kept up with some habits. I wanted to keep up my streak even though I was "on vacation". Your health and levels don't deplete during vacation mode, so you get the 100% health bonus when the mode is turned on. I don't think so many coins should accrue during vacation mode. It feels like cheating to me. I accrued so many coins just with maintaining my habits that I feel like I undermined my progress so far. I did everything I could for a couple months to earn coins to clean up previous rooms, but in the past week I earned several hundred coins just by keeping vacation mode on and doing only 2 habits. I feel cheated because it was so easy earning coins while keeping vacation mode on, so why was I putting in so much effort earlier? Anyway, thank you for the app and I look forward to your next updates!
